the use of homogenized fishnet metasurfaces in a Fabry–Perrot configuration enables the design of highly directive leaky-wave THz antennas.

the use of a homogenized fishnet metasurface is particularly suitable for designing leaky-wave Fabry–Perots in the THz frequency range, with directivities ranging from ∼ 15 to ∼ 30 dB, and with a good agreement with analytical and numerical models.
we propose a systematic design for leaky-wave antennas in the THz frequency range, which can be used for the design of high-directivity antennas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of THz leaky-wave antennas based on homogenized metasmurfaces.
the design of efficient and versatile THz radiating elements based on leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) and on homogenized metatronics.
the systematic and accurate design of efficient THZ leaky-wave Fabry-Perot cavity antennas.

the leaky-wave design approach, well established and consolidated at microwave frequencies, has been successfully extended to THz frequencies, where the design of efficient radiating devices is still a challenging task, due to the intrinsic difficulty of the design process, the technological constraints, the high sensitivity to the manufacturing tolerances, the lack of standardization, and the absence of reliable and accurate numerical tools.

the proposed systematic design is an effective and powerful method for the synthesis of efficient leaky-wave antennas based on homogenized metamaterials, and that the THz range is a very promising field for the application of such leaky-wave devices.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose an efficient and reliable approach for the design and optimization of THz leaky-wave antennas based on the use of homogenized metamaterial surfaces, and that we demonstrate that a specific fish-netlike metasurface is particularly suitable for achieving the desired performance.
the proposed design approach allows the systematic design of efficient THZ radiating devices with directivities ranging from about 20 to 30 dB.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the THz band, the leaky-wave concept can be successfully exploited to design highly directive antennas, with directivities of the same order of those achievable at microwave frequencies, and that the proposed systematic design approach can be used to achieve the desired directivities.
the proposed leaky-wave approach can be used to design THz antennas with high directivity, which is a key requirement for THz imaging and sensing applications.

the leaky-wave design approach is not only applicable to planar antennas but it can also be extended to Fabry–Perrot cavity antennas, with significant advantages in terms of efficiency and directivity.
